title: Runly stack manifest (runly.yml; backlot.yml and stack.yaml accepted)
description: What a repo declares so runly can broker environments for it. Everything {{...}} is injected by the engine (symbolic ports, datastore URLs, service URLs). Policy (pool sizes, TTLs, substrates) never lives here.

name.description: Stack identity; pools are keyed by repo + this name.

services.description: Supervised shell commands, one per service. Commands, not containers.

appliances.description: Singular, machine-shared backing services (a Postgres server, a Redis) that environments point at but never own. Ensured (probe -> start once machine-wide -> wait), never supervised, never stopped automatically.

builds.description: How one `up` runs its services' builds. `parallel` (default): in depends_on waves — a build runs after the builds of what its service depends on, and the builds of one wave run at once (the load budget holds their summed resources). `serial`: one at a time, in manifest order — for builds that share an output or a lock the build tool does not handle.

caches.description: Build and install output inside the worktree (node_modules, **/obj, .angular, ...). Environments run in the worktree (decision 0032), so this is what is NOT source: an upkeep `when:` glob never matches it. runly never deletes it.

keep.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored: since decision 0032 there is no environment-side reset for it to protect files from.

include.description: Git-ignored files that still count as source (.env.local), so an upkeep `when:` glob can match them.

outputs.description: Accepted and ignored since decision 0032: it listed files `runly run` reported as changed, and `runly run` was removed. Build outputs that decide a restart are declared per service (`services.<name>.outputs`).

upkeep.description: Closed list of fingerprint->action rules, run at bind time in order (decision 0008).

logins.description: Seeded login(s) consumers may use. Dev-grade by definition. A single object is one login; a list declares several, and the FIRST is the primary one `ctx.logins` reports.

token.description: Command minting an auth token; {{role}} available. Must print JSON.

checks.description: Accepted and ignored since decision 0032: `runly run` was removed. A manifest that still declares checks loads, with a one-line deprecation warning; repo scripts read the environment from `runly ctx --env` instead.

forbidden.description: When true, `runly preview` is refused (work-error). Stacks with fixed dev credentials must set this.

publisher.description: Named preview publisher adapter (default: cloudflare-quick). Known: cloudflare-quick, cloudflare-named, tailscale (tailnet-only HTTPS via `tailscale serve`).

domain.description: Zone a naming publisher publishes under, e.g. example.dev. Required by cloudflare-named; ignored by cloudflare-quick.

prefix.description: What makes a hostname this environment's own (<service>-<prefix>.<domain>). Unset means the environment id, which is unique by construction; set it only to pin a memorable name, and only where one environment of this stack runs at a time.

https_port.description: tailscale publisher only: the HTTPS port on this machine's tailnet name. Unset means a port derived from the environment id and service, stable for the environment's lifetime. Pin it only where one environment of this stack publishes at a time; ignored by the Cloudflare publishers.

role.description: The role this login stands for, matching the {{role}} an `auth.token` hook takes. Informational.

description.description: What this login is FOR — the scope or permissions it exercises, so a consumer can pick the right one without reading the seed.

run.description: The supervised process. Daemon is its parent. Executes under `sh` (dash on Ubuntu, bash-as-sh on macOS) — write POSIX sh, no bashisms.

when.description: Globs (relative to the stack root, git-listed, minus caches:) of what the build reads. When none of the matched files changed (path, size, mtime) since the last SUCCESSFUL build of this service in this worktree, the build is skipped and `up` says so; `up --rebuild` forces it (decision 0038).

serial.description: Run this build alone, never at the same time as another service's build. By default the builds of services that do not depend on each other run at once (depends_on waves).

build.description: String form: run on every `up` that starts or keeps this service, and on every `runly warm` — runly keeps no build cache; the build tool decides what is current (decision 0032). Object form `{run, when}`: skipped while its `when:` files are unchanged since the last successful build (decision 0038). Executes under `sh` (dash on Ubuntu, bash-as-sh on macOS) — write POSIX sh, no bashisms.

compare.description: stat: path, size and mtime (default). content: hash the files, so a build that rewrites identical files does not restart the service.

outputs.description: Globs (relative to the stack root) of what `build:` produces, e.g. `backend/host/Fid.Host/bin/**` or `dist/web-audit`. Every `up` snapshots them around the build and restarts this service only when they changed. Without it, a service with a build is restarted after every build (decision 0032). The object form chooses how they are compared (decision 0038).

watch_run.description: Accepted and ignored since decision 0032 (`--watch` was removed); the service always runs `run:`.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the repo root.

port.description: Symbolic port name; the engine allocates a public port (held by the daemon's proxy) and starts the service on an internal one. In this service's own run/env, {{ports.<name>}} is the internal port to listen on; everywhere else it is the public port ({{public_ports.<name>}} is always public). Omit for portless services (workers).

env_from.description: Allowlisted caller environment inputs. `up` refreshes values from its caller; reset-data retains the lease's inputs. A supplied value overrides a same-named env entry; a missing optional input keeps an explicit env default, otherwise masks the daemon value. Memory only: re-run up after a daemon restart.

fatal_logs.description: ERE of log markers that fail a boot in seconds instead of polling readiness to timeout.

depends_on.description: Services that must be ready before this one starts.

hot_reload.description: Accepted and ignored since decision 0032 (`sync` was removed). Whether an `up` restarts a running service is decided by its build `outputs:`; a service without a build keeps running.

idle.description: How long this service may go without client bytes through its public port and without a runly verb on its environment before it is stopped; the next connection starts it again (decision 0035). A duration (90s, 10m, 2h), seconds as a number, or `never`. Default BACKLOT_SERVICE_IDLE_MS (10 minutes).

http.description: Path polled on the service's port until 200.

log.description: ERE that must appear in the service log (portless services).

server.description: runly never runs datastore servers; it probes them.

probe.description: host:port TCP-probed before anything starts (server drivers). Failure is an infra-error, never code blame.

url.description: Connection-string template handed to services and `runly ctx --env`; {{ns}} available. Required for server drivers; ignored for sqlite (the ns IS the file path).

create.description: Repo command that creates+seeds a namespace; {{ns}} and {{preset}} available.

drop.description: Repo command that drops a namespace; {{ns}} available. Best-effort (run before restore and on recycle).

template_restore.description: Repo command that clones a baked template namespace into a fresh one; {{template}} and {{ns}} available (e.g. postgres: createdb -T {{template}} {{ns}}). When present, `create` bakes once per seed-content hash and every bind restores in seconds.

default_preset.description: The preset a datastore is created with when none is named. A name; the pre-0.13 {run, session} form is still accepted (session wins, then run).

template.description: sqlite only: bake a template file per seed-content hash and restore by copy. Server drivers use template_restore instead.

list.description: Repo command printing the namespaces ({{ns}} values) of this datastore that exist on its server, one per line. Read only by `runly pool doctor`: a listed name in runly's naming (backlot_...) that no journal row or template marker references is an orphan, which `--fix` drops with `drop:` (decision 0037).

when.description: A file path or glob(...) whose content hash triggers the rule (direction-agnostic per-env ledger).

run.description: Repo command, or an engine built-in prefixed with @ (e.g. @rebake-template <datastore>).

timeout.description: Command deadline in seconds (default 300). BACKLOT_CMD_TIMEOUT_S overrides this value.

probe.description: host:port TCP-probed; reachability IS the appliance's identity — whoever answers is the appliance, no matter who started it.

start.description: Daemonizing repo command (e.g. docker run -d ...) run ONCE machine-wide when the probe fails. Absent = today's behavior: unreachable is an infra-error you resolve yourself.

stop.description: Repo command for the explicit `runly appliance stop` verb. Never run automatically — appliances are durable; heat is the point.

ready.description: Optional readiness gate polled after TCP accepts (exit 0 = ready), e.g. pg_isready — TCP-accept alone can precede real readiness.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait after start for probe (and ready:) to pass before infra-error.

resources.description: What the appliance costs while running; counted against the load budget when an `up` would start it (decision 0036). Its build: entry is ignored.

size.description: A size: bytes as a number, or a string with a K/M/G/T suffix (600M, 2G, 1.5GiB).

resources.description: What this costs the box, for the server-wide load budget (decision 0036). Left out = a conservative default (run 512M / 0.5 cpu; build 1G / 1 cpu), which `runly plan` says it assumed.

build.description: What its `build:` costs while it runs; held only while building.
